summary.headline: Premiums still growing fast, but nine-month profit collapsed to Rs 158mn; fair value cut to about Rs 16
summary.text: Janashakthi Insurance (JINS.N0000) is a life insurer, 74% owned by Janashakthi PLC, that also owns 25% of First Capital Holdings. This full rebuild from the four CSE reports keeps the business picture but lowers the value. Premiums are still growing fast (up 20.9% to Rs 7.42bn in nine months of 2026), capital is very strong (CAR 284% at December 2025, minimum 120%) and there has been a profit every year for ten years. But nine-month profit fell to Rs 158mn from Rs 2.79bn (EPS Rs 0.23 against Rs 4.11): rising bond yields turned fair value gains of Rs 1.55bn into a Rs 374mn loss, and First Capital Holdings swung to a Rs 424mn loss. The year-end transfer from the life fund (Rs 477mn last year) will add to the full year, and no dividend has been paid in 2026 so far. At Rs 37.90 it trades at 1.53x NAV of Rs 24.73 and 31x trailing earnings. On normal profit of about Rs 2.0bn (Rs 2.95 a share, a 12% return on equity, below the 16.5% cost of equity from the house formula), four methods put fair value at Rs 16.06, down from Rs 24.60, so the price is more than twice fair value. Buy up to Rs 13.65; Rs 12.05 or less is a strong buy. It stays on the watch list: still a good business on three of the four tests, but the return-on-equity pass is now at risk.

quality.reason: Strong capital, a profit every year and cash dividends; returns were high in 2023–2025 but came mostly from investment gains, and 2026 is weak.

tests.label: Return on equity of 15% or more
tests.note: On average equity: 8.5% (2021), 12.9% (2022), 31.3% (2023), 27.8% (2024), 20.7% (2025), five-year average about 20%. The twelve months to September 2026 give about 5% (profit Rs 0.83bn) before the year-end surplus transfer. Passes on the several-year record, but a 2026 ROE below about 8% would turn this into a fail at the next update.

tests.label: Capital comfortably above the minimum (insurer)
tests.note: Risk-based CAR 284% at December 2025 (277% a year earlier) against a 120% minimum and a 160% intervention level; available capital Rs 14.3bn. Borrowings Rs 1.22bn at September 2026 (Rs 1.62bn in December), a Seylan Bank term loan secured on the First Capital Holdings shares.

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: No loss in ten years, but profit swings with investment gains and the actuary's surplus transfer: realised and fair value gains Rs 2.90bn (2024), Rs 1.78bn (2025), −Rs 0.38bn (nine months of 2026); surplus Rs 1.79bn (2024), Rs 0.48bn (2025). Nine-month profit fell 94% to Rs 158mn.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: (Long-run ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth) × NAV Rs 24.73: 0.43x / 0.70x / 1.22x book, with ROE 10% / 13% / 17% and growth 4% / 5% / 6%. A long-run ROE below the 16.5% cost of equity is worth less than book.

models.name: P/E method (justified)
models.comment: 2027 EPS Rs 1.90 / 2.95 / 3.90 (normal profit about Rs 1.3bn / 2.0bn / 2.65bn) × the justified P/E at the cost of equity, payout 1 − g ÷ ROE: 4.3x / 5.4x / 7.2x. All three are above the Rs 1.22 run-rate, which has no year-end surplus transfer in it; 2025's EPS without investment gains was about Rs 2.9.

models.name: Dividend model
models.comment: Next year's dividend Rs 1.00 / 1.75 / 2.55 (53–65% of 2027 EPS), growing 0% / 0.4% / 0.4% for five years (capped at the 0.4% supported by 2025's 98% payout), then the payout becomes 1 − g ÷ ROE with growth 4% / 5% / 6%.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Used instead of a cash-flow DCF, which doesn't suit an insurer. Book Rs 24.73 plus profit above the cost of equity: ROE moves in a straight line from 11.9% to 10% / 13% / 17% over ten years with a 60% payout, then the excess return grows at 4% / 5% / 6%.

modelsNote: An insurer's cash flows are mostly premiums and policy reserves, so instead of a cash-flow DCF I used residual income and a justified price to book, alongside P/E and dividends, all at the 16.5% cost of equity (18.0% / 15.0% bear / bull) and all worked by scripts/valuation.py. Growth check: dividend growth of 0% / 0.4% / 0.4% for five years against 0.4% supported (2.0% of 2025 profit kept × 20.5% ROE); all within 2 points. Long-run growth of 4–6% stays below the 12.24% bond yield and is paid for by the profit kept (1 − g ÷ ROE). Every method lands below book value because normal ROE (13% base) is below the cost of equity.

scenarios.common: Cost of equity from the house formula (risk-free 8.24% + beta 0.80 × 10.28% equity premium). Normal profit is 2025's profit before tax without realised and fair value gains (Rs 2.17bn), taxed at about the 2025 rate; bear assumes First Capital Holdings contributes nothing, bull a larger life-fund surplus. 679.6m shares after the April 2026 split. Stated under SLFRS 4; SLFRS 17 may change book value and the timing of profit.

higher: A large year-end surplus transfer and full-year 2026 profit well above Rs 1bn.
First Capital Holdings back to profit and paying dividends again.
An embedded value or SLFRS 17 contractual service margin disclosure showing the in-force life book is worth much more than book value.

Further losses at First Capital Holdings, a primary dealer exposed to bond yields.
Claims growing faster than premiums (net claims +37.8% against premiums +20.9% in nine months).
A small or no dividend for 2026.

fullText:
**Janashakthi Insurance PLC (JINS.N0000): full rebuild, 21 November 2026**

**Summary.** A fast-growing, well-capitalised life insurer whose profit still depends on bond and share markets. Nine-month 2026 profit fell to Rs 158mn (EPS Rs 0.23) from Rs 2.79bn, even though premiums rose 20.9%. On normal profit of about Rs 2.0bn a year (EPS Rs 2.95, ROE about 12%) and the house cost of equity of 16.5%, fair value is **Rs 16.06** (was Rs 24.60). Buy up to **Rs 13.65**, strong buy at **Rs 12.05** or less. At Rs 37.90 (CSE close, 20 November 2026) the share is more than twice fair value. Category 2, watch list: three of four business tests pass, but the returns test is at risk.

**What changed in this rebuild.** All four reports were read again from the CSE downloads: the 2025 annual report and the March, June and September 2026 interims. The record now keeps only printed figures, with every quarter and comparative column. The cost of equity now comes from the house formula (beta 0.80, 16.5%) instead of a hand-set 17.5%. Normal profit is lowered from Rs 2.7bn to Rs 2.0bn, because 2026 has shown how much of 2023–2025's profit came from investment gains. Long-run ROE falls from 16% to 13% (base). Management plans and the shareholder list are new.

**The business.** Janashakthi Life sells life policies through 76 branches. Profit has three sources: (1) the surplus the actuary releases from the life fund to shareholders at year end (Rs 1.79bn in 2024, Rs 0.48bn in 2025); (2) returns on the shareholders' investments, including realised and fair value gains (Rs 2.90bn in 2024, Rs 1.78bn in 2025, a Rs 0.38bn loss in nine months of 2026); and (3) its 25% share of First Capital Holdings (profit Rs 1.33bn in 2024, Rs 0.94bn in 2025, a Rs 0.42bn loss in nine months of 2026). Interim results have no surplus transfer, so they always understate the year.

**Latest results (nine months to September 2026).**
- Gross written premium Rs 7.42bn, up 20.9% (first-year Rs 5.05bn, renewals Rs 2.38bn). The third quarter fell 2.6%.
- Net claims up 37.8% to Rs 3.59bn. Acquisition costs 28.1% of premium, administrative costs 18.3%.
- Investment income Rs 2.45bn (−6.7%), fair value loss Rs 374mn (gain Rs 1.55bn), First Capital share of loss Rs 424mn (profit Rs 1.01bn).
- Profit before tax Rs 391mn (Rs 3.09bn); profit Rs 158mn (Rs 2.79bn). Q3 alone: Rs 29mn (Rs 1.48bn).
- Equity Rs 16.80bn, NAV Rs 24.73; borrowings Rs 1.22bn; life fund Rs 19.72bn. No dividend paid in 2026.

**Valuation (Rs a share).**

| Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Justified price to book | 10.60 | 17.20 | 30.23 | 17.83 |
| P/E (justified) | 8.14 | 15.79 | 28.04 | 15.95 |
| Dividend model | 6.83 | 13.55 | 23.62 | 13.55 |
| Residual income | 11.63 | 16.40 | 26.17 | 16.92 |
| Average | 9.30 | 15.74 | 27.02 | **16.06** |

Weights 30/50/20. Buy price = fair value less 15% (Rs 13.65); strong buy less 25% (Rs 12.05).

**Assumptions.**
- Cost of equity 18.0% / 16.5% / 15.0%: 8.24% risk-free + beta 0.80 × 10.28% (Damodaran's global life-insurance beta; provisional). No WACC or DCF for an insurer.
- Normal 2027 profit Rs 1.3bn / 2.0bn / 2.65bn (EPS Rs 1.90 / 2.95 / 3.90). Base is 2025's profit before tax without investment gains (Rs 2.17bn), after tax. All three are above the Rs 1.22 twelve-month run-rate, which has no surplus transfer in it.
- Long-run ROE 10% / 13% / 17%; long-run growth 4% / 5% / 6% (below the 12.24% bond yield).
- Dividends Rs 1.00 / 1.75 / 2.55 next year (about 60% of profit), growing 0–0.4% for five years. That is capped at the 0.4% growth that 2025's 98% payout supports; after that the payout is 1 − g ÷ ROE.
- Growth check: assumed 0% / 0.4% / 0.4%, supported 0.4%: all within 2 points.

**Ratio checks.** Beta 0.80 and cost of equity 16.5% are inside the normal ranges. The justified P/E is 4.3–7.2x; the market's 31x trailing (12.8x on normal EPS) is far above it. A justified P/B below 1x follows from a long-run ROE below the cost of equity. The 2025 dividend (98% of profit) was above what the business can keep paying, so the dividend is at risk.

**Business tests (3 of 4, good).**
- Returns: pass, but at risk. ROE was 8.5%, 12.9%, 31.3%, 27.8% and 20.7% in 2021–2025, and about 5% in the twelve months to September 2026.
- Capital: pass, CAR 284% against a 120% minimum.
- Steady profit: fail. There was no loss in ten years, but profit swings with gains, the surplus transfer and First Capital.
- Cash and dividends: pass, with Rs 3.40bn paid for 2025 and Rs 3.00bn for 2024.

The category stays 2 (watch list). If 2026's full-year ROE comes in under about 8%, it would fall to 3.

**Management.** The Chairperson and CEO promise growth above the industry, a five-year growth plan, digital tools and AI, preparation for SLFRS 17, and asset–liability management against rate swings. Premium growth and cost ratios are on track. The rate-swing promise was missed in 2026: fair value losses and investment income cut nine-month profit by 94%.

**Shareholders.** Janashakthi PLC owns 74.24%, First Capital Limited 5.78% and Mr Y S H I Silva 3.21%. The public holds 19.97% (8,777 holders) and no director holds shares. The September quarter brought only small purchases.

**Buy plan (500 shares).** Buy 200 at up to Rs 13.65, 150 at Rs 12.85 and 150 at Rs 12.05: average Rs 12.93, about Rs 6,465. Not realistic soon: the 2026 low is Rs 37.50, and on today's shares the price was last this low in 2024.

**What would change the view.** Higher: a large year-end surplus, First Capital back in profit, an embedded value or SLFRS 17 CSM figure showing the in-force book is worth well above book, or lower bond yields. Lower: a weak full-year 2026 (returns test fails), an SLFRS 17 hit to equity, more First Capital losses, claims outgrowing premiums, or a small 2026 dividend.

**Uncertain.**
- The beta is provisional: one global sector figure and only one local 5-year beta.
- There is no embedded value, and the interims give no capital adequacy ratio.
- The SLFRS 17 impact isn't quantified.
- Q1 2026 EPS and NAV were printed before the split.

requiredReturn.betaBasis: Provisional. An insurer, so the sector's levered beta is used without relevering: Damodaran's January 2026 global Insurance (Life) levered beta 0.80 (143 firms; from a web-search extract, as his emerging-markets file couldn't be opened from this run). Only one local 5-year beta was found (StockAnalysis 0.49), not the three the rule needs, and the float is small (19.97%), so the higher figure, 0.80, is used. Refresh in January 2027.

Asset–liability management to absorb interest-rate swings
